recommended.title: The application serves itself on loopback, hardened, as a standalone sidecar
recommended.acceptance: The desktop target builds a Next standalone server that a shell can spawn, and every control docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 7 names is implemented and tested. REQUIRED: output 'standalone' is set for the desktop target and only for it -- the document specifies it in two places and next.config.ts sets it in none, which is the single largest gap between the recorded design and the code. REQUIRED: the server binds 127.0.0.1 explicitly and never 0.0.0.0, asserted by a test rather than by configuration alone, because Next reads HOSTNAME from the environment and an inherited value would silently expose the listener to the LAN. REQUIRED: a per-launch 256-bit CSPRNG bearer token passed through the environment, required on every request, with a constant-time comparison and a refusal that does not state whether the token was absent or wrong. REQUIRED: Host header validation against the exact expected literal, because a bearer token does not stop DNS rebinding. REQUIRED: the application emits its own Content-Security-Policy, because Tauri's CSP injection stops applying the moment the frontend is a URL rather than bundled assets -- this is a real loss the document names and nothing currently replaces it. REQUIRED: the sidecar reports its actually-bound port on stdout rather than being told which port to use; a pick-then-bind handshake is a TOCTOU race and is refused. NOT IN SCOPE: the Rust shell, which is PW-0102.
